acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

header.reason: Angela, the COO, signed with Adyen after a store operations workshop where we described a till return instead of showing it, had no one who had run a store rollout, and said a partner would do installs. Tom names Raj as decider and points to the web side, but the store side is what decided it.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Lead store messaging with the broken cross-channel return: an online order the store can't see or refund at the till.
findings.quote: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Arm reps to reach the COO beyond kickoff with a single-accountable-vendor story covering store installs and support, not partner handoffs.
findings.quote: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Pre-empt a retail-team pitch by introducing our store rollout people early; this rests on Raj's secondhand account, so confirm what Adyen showed.
findings.quote: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Cut the 'line between them has pretty much disappeared' slide; keep the online checkout demo and add a step-by-step till return walkthrough.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a ready-to-call store-and-online retailer reference and a sample multi-store rollout plan covering dates, installers and old tills.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'the tills' and 'one system for the tills and the website' instead of 'point of sale' and 'unified commerce'.
findings.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
